reasoning: Recent polling over the last several weeks shows a very tight Texas U.S. Senate race, with most high‑quality polls giving Democrat James Talarico a small lead over Republican Ken Paxton, but at least one recent Emerson poll has Paxton narrowly ahead; overall, the current snapshot is essentially a toss‑up with a slight D edge in the Senate polling average. Structurally, however, Texas remains an R‑leaning state (Cook PVI R+4), so any Democratic advantage in current Senate polls is modest and contingent, and there is insufficient recent, state‑specific general‑election presidential polling within the last 45 days to justify a separate presidential margin estimate.

sources.name: USA Today summary of Texas Public Opinion Research poll
sources.details: Texas Public Opinion Research (TPOR) poll of 1,048 likely Texas voters found James Talarico at 45% and Ken Paxton at 40%, a Talarico +5 Senate lead several months before Election Day.

sources.name: USA Today summary of Fox News Texas Senate poll
sources.details: Fox News statewide poll of 1,006 registered Texas voters found Talarico 51% and Paxton 48%, a Talarico +3 U.S. Senate lead, noting the margin is within the poll’s ±3% sampling error.

sources.name: USA Today summary of Texas Southern University Senate poll
sources.details: Texas Southern University’s Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center poll of 1,200 likely voters showed Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 45%, a Talarico +2 Senate lead within the ±2.83% margin of error.

sources.name: Houston Public Media on TSU Barbara Jordan Center poll
sources.details: Houston Public Media report on the Texas Southern University poll likewise notes Talarico leading Paxton 47% to 45% in the Texas U.S. Senate race, a 2‑point Democratic edge.

sources.name: The Hill on TSU Barbara Jordan Center Texas Senate poll
sources.details: The Hill’s coverage of the Texas Southern University poll reports Talarico leading Paxton 47% to 45% among likely Texas voters, describing Paxton as trailing by 2 points in the closely watched U.S. Senate race.

sources.name: Axios on TSU Texas Senate poll and streak of Talarico leads
sources.details: Axios notes that three consecutive Texas Senate polls have shown Talarico narrowly ahead of Paxton, highlighting the TSU survey with Talarico up 47%-45% and framing it as a slim Democratic lead.

sources.name: New York Post on Fox News poll and RealClearPolitics Texas Senate average
sources.details: New York Post story cites the Fox News Texas Senate poll showing Talarico 51% and Paxton 48% (D+3) and notes that Talarico has a 0.9‑point edge over Paxton in the latest RealClearPolitics polling aggregate for the race.

sources.name: Texas Tribune summary of recent Texas Senate polls
sources.details: Texas Tribune’s tracking of the U.S. Senate race notes that a latest survey has Paxton leading by one point, breaking a streak of several polls that had shown Talarico with a slight advantage, underscoring the race’s competitiveness.

sources.name: UT Texas Politics Project Senate poll tracker (Emerson College entry)
sources.details: University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll tracker lists an Emerson College Texas Senate poll with Paxton 47%, Talarico 46%, and Paxton +1 spread among 1,000 likely voters.

sources.name: UT Texas Politics Project Senate poll tracker (Bush School/Recon MR entry)
sources.details: UT Texas Politics Project poll tracker also catalogues Bush School/Recon MR poll (Talarico 47%, Paxton 43%, D+4), TSU/YouGov (Talarico 47%, Paxton 45%, D+2), and Fox News (Talarico 51%, Paxton 48%, D+3) showing small Democratic leads in the Texas Senate race.

sources.name: Emerson College Texas 2026 poll release (Senate race)
sources.details: Emerson College’s own release on its Texas 2026 poll describes the U.S. Senate contest between Paxton and Talarico as deadlocked, with topline numbers essentially matching a Paxton +1 result within the ±3% credibility interval.

sources.name: Fox 7 Austin overview of latest Paxton vs. Talarico Senate polls
sources.details: Fox 7 Austin compilation article explains that recent polling shows the 2026 Texas U.S. Senate race as a dead heat, summarizing multiple surveys with slight leads for each candidate and emphasizing the contest’s toss‑up nature.

sources.name: Federal News Network on Texas Senate prediction market odds
sources.details: Federal News Network coverage of prediction markets on the Texas Senate race reports traders currently favor Paxton, with his implied odds around 57% versus Talarico in the low‑to‑mid 40s, indicating markets slightly lean Republican despite recent Democratic poll leads.

sources.name: Cook Political Report State Partisan Voting Index (Texas)
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s state PVI table lists Texas as R+4 at the statewide level, indicating the state votes about four points more Republican than the national average in recent presidential elections.
